content.text: I fixed the bug by changing one entry in `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 passed). `from_roman` checks input against a lookup table, `_TABLE`, which is built by running `_to_roman` over 1–3999. That function works from the symbol list `_VALS`, which paired 900 with the long form `"DCCCC"` instead of the standard subtractive `"CM"`. So every value containing 900 (900–999, 1900–1999, and so on) went into the table in the non-standard form. Valid input like `"CM"` or `"MCMXCIV"` was then rejected as "not a strict Roman numeral". Changing that entry to `(900, "CM")` makes the table hold the standard form for every number from 1 to 3999. The strict check still works as intended: it only accepts standard numerals, so long forms like `"DCCCC"` are now rejected.
